name: Carolina Solar Energy III, LLC
old_description: An architect emeritus, building contractor, solar installer and real estate developer, Richard founded CSE in 2004. Through his leadership, CSE built the first utility-scale solar energy project in the Southeast in 2007. Richard is a lead policy advocate in NC for renewable energy and energy efficiency, past Chair of the NC Sustainable Energy Association and founder of the Carolinas Clean Energy Business Association.
about:
Carolina Solar Energy was founded in 2004 in Durham, North Carolina, by Richard Harkrader, an architect emeritus, building contractor, and real estate developer. The family-owned business began with a goal to demonstrate that renewable energy portfolio standards could build a solar industry in the state. Richard’s early trial-and-error project development led to the first utility-scale solar project in the Southeast, completed at NC State in 2007.

The company develops utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) solar projects across the Southeast and Gulf South, managing site selection, interconnection applications, state permitting, and community outreach. As of the latest figures, over 950 MWdc of projects are operating or under construction. The team handles landowner relations, project management, and policy advocacy, working with municipal partners, utilities, and landowners to bring projects from concept to operation.

Carolina Solar Energy serves utilities, municipal governments, county economic development agencies, and multi-generational landowners in the Southern and Gulf South regions. Notable partners include the City of Raleigh, which completed its first major solar development with the company, and Person County, which hosts three photovoltaic facilities totaling approximately five megawatts. The firm also collaborates with clean energy membership organizations on state and national policy.

The company was started to prove that legislative frameworks could create a viable solar market in North Carolina, and it continues to emphasize early-market entry and community acceptance. Leadership highlights a balance of renewable energy expertise, engineering, installation capability, and financial knowledge as differentiators, along with a rehabilitative workforce partnership with TROSA.

Carolina Woodworks operates from Lyman, South Carolina, in the Upstate region. The family-owned shop draws on more than 30 years of hands-on experience and multi-generational woodworking knowledge, with a background in custom home building that informs its approach to cabinetry and millwork.

The company designs, builds, finishes, and installs fully custom cabinetry, built-ins, vanities, entertainment walls, commercial millwork, and architectural details. Every project is fabricated in-house using premium materials, BLUM soft-close hardware, dovetailed drawer boxes, and professional lacquer finishes. The shop works across frameless, face-frame, inset, and multiple overlay cabinet configurations.

Carolina Woodworks serves homeowners, builders, remodelers, interior designers, and commercial clients throughout the Upstate. Its portfolio includes custom kitchens, bathrooms, built-in shelving, entertainment centers, office suites, and pantry systems for both residential and commercial spaces.

The firm emphasizes exact-design flexibility—building each piece around the home's architecture rather than a catalog—along with technical range that covers multiple cabinet styles under one roof. Furniture-grade execution, precision joinery, specialized finishes, and direct client communication with visible progress are cited as core differentiators.

name: Carolina Yarn & Fabrics Inc
old_description: Carolina Yarn and Fabrics, LLC, based in Laurens, SC, is a leading manufacturer and principal supplier of highly engineered fabric-formed concrete erosion control and scour protection systems. These systems have been utilized for more than 40 years around the world.
about:
Carolina Yarn and Fabrics, LLC, based in Laurens, South Carolina, has been a manufacturer and principal supplier of highly engineered fabric-formed concrete erosion control and scour protection systems since the ARMORFORM® trade name was established in 1984. The company draws together teams of project managers, engineers, and production and field service managers dedicated to sustainable solutions.

The firm produces ARMORFORM® fabric-formed concrete systems, which use double-layer woven geo-textiles engineered exclusively as forms for casting concrete erosion control revetments and linings. The geo-textiles are woven from polyester and/or nylon yarns and designed with specific mechanical and hydraulic properties. Installation involves positioning the fabric forms and pumping high-strength, fine-aggregate concrete, either underwater or on dry land. By 2002, more than 50 million square feet of ARMORFORM® had been installed worldwide, including projects inside the Arctic Circle and at the Olmsted Locks and Dam on the Ohio River.

The company serves engineering firms, government agencies, and commercial clients across infrastructure, water, environment, industry, and energy sectors. Notable references include acceptance by the Mine Safety and Health Administration for mining facilities in 1993, U.S. Navy approval for underwater ballast and protection of pipelines and communication cables in 2002, and exclusive collaboration with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers on scour protection for the Olmsted Locks and Dam in 2008.

Carolina Yarn and Fabrics emphasizes engineered products, comprehensive technical support, and responsive delivery, which the company says have resulted in most projects being repeat work with long-standing clients. The focus on sustainable solutions for infrastructure, water, environment, industry, and energy underpins its approach.

name: Carpenter Co
old_description: Carpenter Co. is the world’s largest vertically integrated manufacturer of polyurethane foams, and serves a diversified global marketplace with polyurethane chemical solutions, polyester fibers, and insulation materials through a network of more than 60 production locations.
about:
Carpenter Co. is headquartered in Moore, Oklahoma, and traces its origins to 1950 when it began as a local latex foam manufacturer. The company has since grown into the world's largest vertically integrated producer of polyurethane foams, operating a network of more than 60 production locations worldwide. Ownership details such as family or veteran status are not publicly disclosed.

The company manufactures polyurethane chemical solutions, polyester fibers, and insulation materials, with a core focus on flexible urethane foams. Its vertical integration includes production of polyether polyols, a key foam component. Carpenter employs approximately 6,500 people globally and backs its operations with state-of-the-art research and development facilities in Richmond, where expert teams design innovative products and conduct rigorous in-house testing.

Carpenter serves a diversified global marketplace, with a highlighted focus on the medical field through tailored protection solutions. Its products also support bedding and furniture applications, as evidenced by the patent-pending Casper Core+ technology aimed at improving mattress recyclability. The company's domestic mattress manufacturing operations are noted to support American jobs and local communities.

Carpenter emphasizes purpose-driven operations guided by a code of conduct and environmental stewardship. The company says its differentiation lies in its vertically integrated model, global footprint, and commitment to innovation, recognized by the 2026 Center for the Polyurethanes Industry Polyurethane Innovation Award for Casper Core+ technology.

name: Catamount Solar
old_description: At Catamount Solar, we deliver the advantages of solar energy to all of our commercial and residential  customers. Our employee-owners have a strong commitment to delivering the best possible renewable energy solutions to our customers every day. We bring decades of skill, experience, and enthusiasm to both residential and commercial solar. We provide good-paying jobs and profit sharing to our member owners. And we donate 5% of our profits to local community organizations.
about:
Catamount Solar was founded in 2011 in Randolph, Vermont, as a worker-owned cooperative. The company operates under an employee-ownership model in which all workers are either cooperative members or on a defined path to membership, giving each installer a direct stake in the business.

The cooperative specializes in the design and installation of solar photovoltaic systems for residential, commercial, and agricultural customers, as well as off-grid and battery-backup solutions. Its crews handle everything from site evaluation and system engineering to permitting, installation, and ongoing service, drawing on decades of combined field experience.

Clients range from individual homeowners and family farms to businesses and institutions such as Crossett Brook Middle School in Duxbury. The company serves the broader New England region with a focus on Vermont, helping customers reduce reliance on utility power and lower long-term energy costs.

Catamount Solar distinguishes itself through its ownership structure, which the company says reduces turnover and ensures that experienced technicians remain on staff for the life of a system’s warranty. It also commits five percent of annual profits to Vermont community and environmental programs, reinforcing a mission that extends beyond energy production.

name: Central Carolina Plastics Inc
about:
Central Carolina Products, Inc. was founded in 1993 in Burlington, North Carolina. The company is privately held, certified as a minority-owned business, and has been family-owned and operated since its inception.

The firm operates as a custom injection molder of thermoplastics, offering secondary assembly, decorative coating, design and development support, and tooling services. Its production floor houses 61 microprocessor-controlled presses ranging from 40 to 1,650 tons, equipped for scientific molding, insert molding, over molding, hot oil molding, and sequential valve gate control. Robotic extraction, custom end-of-arm tooling, and automated material handling with silo storage support the operation. A new facility was built in 2003 and a second plant acquired in 2008.

Customers span the automotive and industrial sectors, with documented relationships including General Motors, Lear Corporation, IAC, Stanley Black & Decker, Xylem, Tower Components, and GBF, Inc. The company also references alignment with Automotive Industry Action Group standards.

Central Carolina Products emphasizes investment in state-of-the-art equipment and cross-functional teams to analyze design and manufacturing processes, aiming to reduce internal costs and pass savings to customers. It has been recognized three times as Lear Corporation’s Supplier of the Year.

name: Central Kentucky Sonar
old_description: Like most anglers, I started fishing as a kid.  Bluegill fishing with my dad and younger brother.  The passion has stayed with me my whole life.  Being a weekend warrior in my first boat, didn't give me enough time on the water to learn my electronics.  I didn't know where to go or who to ask for help, even though electronics were much simpler then.  So I started Central Kentucky Sonar to help people learn as much as possible with hands on teaching.
about:
Central Kentucky Sonar operates from Nicholasville, Kentucky. The business was established in 2018 by an avid angler who grew up bluegill fishing with his father and younger brother. After struggling to learn marine electronics on his own as a weekend boater, he founded the company to provide hands-on instruction for others facing the same challenge.

The company functions as a full-service marine electronics retailer. It sells fish-finding and navigation units, handles professional installation, and then provides personalized training on how to operate the equipment. The service model centers on one-on-one sessions tailored to each customer’s specific unit and fishing style, whether they are new to electronics, switching brands, or seeking to fine-tune existing settings.

The primary clientele are recreational anglers and boaters in the Central Kentucky region. Customers range from beginners needing basic orientation to experienced fishermen looking to maximize the capabilities of advanced sonar and GPS systems. The business also serves as a community partner, acting as an ambassador for the Jessamine County Homeless Coalition and a sponsor of the Jessamine County Food Pantry.

The founder started Central Kentucky Sonar because he found no local resource for learning electronics when he bought his first boat. The company differentiates itself by combining retail sales, installation, and dedicated instruction under one roof, emphasizing a personal, undivided-attention teaching approach rather than classroom-style or remote support.

name: Central Metal Fabricators, Inc.
old_description: Since 1980, Central Metal Fabricators, Inc. has provided innovative design, fabrication, and assembly services to a diverse range of industries. We stock over 800 different parts, and have the documentation to manufacture thousands more.
about:
Central Metal Fabricators, Inc. (CMF) was founded in 1980 in Farmingdale, New Jersey. The company began as a welding and repair shop and has since grown into a designer and fabricator of precision components and assemblies.

CMF operates a 35,000-square-foot manufacturing facility staffed by approximately 25 skilled employees. Its capabilities span design, engineering, rapid prototyping, reverse engineering, and full-scale fabrication. Processes include laser cutting, CNC milling, turning, punching, and bending; manual and CNC machining; MIG and TIG welding; mechanical and electrical assembly; wiring harness manufacturing for high- and low-voltage applications; and industrial sewing for strap assemblies. The company stocks over 800 parts and maintains documentation for thousands more.

The company serves commercial, industrial, military, medical, pharmaceutical, research, and food-preparation industries. Approximately 95 percent of its work supports the United States Armed Forces, including installations such as Aberdeen Proving Ground, Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst, NAVAIR, Naval Surface Warfare Center, Picatinny Arsenal, Tobyhanna Army Depot, and others. The remaining balance serves commercial clients.

CMF highlights a record of no financial defaults, no litigation, no lost-time injuries, and no adverse actions from the EPA, OSHA, or NJDEP. It attributes its longevity to first-class personnel, superior capabilities, and traditional business values.

name: Central Montana Food Hub
old_description: Central Montana Food Hub is your source for high quality local food. Ordering from Central Montana Food Hub helps to build and support our local producers, and to preserve our precious agricultural land for sustainable future use.
about:
Central Montana Food Hub operates from Martinsdale, Montana, as an aggregator and online marketplace for locally grown and produced food. The company connects regional producers with consumers, restaurants, institutions, and retailers across a wide swath of central Montana.

The hub manages an online ordering platform that opens weekly for home delivery and community pickup in towns including Livingston, Big Timber, White Sulphur Springs, Harlowton, and Lewistown. It handles meat, produce, eggs, honey, grains, and other products, providing packaging and delivery logistics for its producer network. Wholesale customers receive customized ordering with recurring options.

The service supplies dining establishments such as Wild Oats Bakery, Jesse Peppers Smoke Shack, The Mint Bar, Musselshell Steakhouse, and Gally’s Brewing Co., as well as grocery stores like Lewistown Town and County, Midtown Market 2, and Castle Mountain Grocery. It also participates in the Harlo Farmers Market and White Sulphur Springs Farmers Market.

The organization states its purpose is to build and support local producers and preserve agricultural land for sustainable use, simplifying the process for farmers to meet demand for local food.
